theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. You may use a calculator unless the instructor says otherwise. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is an appointment system used for in a salon or spa?
options: To count the stock on the shelves at the end of the month
To plan which client sees which worker, for what, and when
To record the wages paid to each worker every week
To list the products each client has bought from the salon

questions.stem: Which details must be taken when booking an appointment?
options: The client's age, job, religion and full home address
Only the client's first name and the day
The client's bank card number and PIN, to hold the booking
Client's name, phone number, service, worker, date and time

questions.stem: Why must the receptionist know how long each service takes?
options: So she books enough time and the worker does not run late
So she can charge clients by the minute
So she can tell clients to arrive an hour early
So she can fit two clients into the same time with one worker

questions.stem: A relaxer touch-up and style takes 2 hours. The client is booked at 10:30 am. When will the stylist be free?
A manicure takes 45 minutes and a pedicure takes 1 hour. A client books both with one technician, starting at 2:15 pm. When will she finish?
A client wants a full set of acrylic nails. Who should she be booked with?
options: Any worker who is free at that time
The receptionist, who knows the client well
A hair stylist who has watched acrylic nails being done before
A nail technician who is trained in acrylic nails

questions.stem: Why should the appointment book show each worker's days off, breaks and training times?
options: So clients are not booked when the worker is not there
So clients waiting at reception can see who works the hardest
So the owner can pay staff less
So staff can swap clients without telling anyone

questions.stem: When booking a chemical service, what is "processing time"?
options: The time it takes the client to pay at the desk
The time it takes to book the appointment by phone
The time a product is left on the hair to work
The time the client waits before her service starts

questions.stem: A new client wants a lash tint on Saturday morning. The maker says a skin test is needed 48 hours before. When should the skin test be booked?
options: On Saturday, just before the tint
On Thursday or earlier
On Friday afternoon
On the Monday after the tint

questions.stem: Why should the result of a skin test be written on the client's record?
options: So staff can see it was done and safe before the service
So the client can be charged for the test
So that the test never needs to be done again, whatever happens
So the supplier knows how much tint was used

questions.stem: After making a booking by phone, what should the receptionist do?
options: Hang up quickly so the line is free
Ask the client to call back to check it
Write it on a scrap of paper to copy into the book later on
Read the details back to the client to confirm them

questions.stem: Why do many salons send a reminder text or call the day before an appointment, if the client has agreed?
options: To ask the client to bring her own towels and products with her
To tell the client the price has gone up
To reduce no-shows and give the client a chance to change it
To check that the client's phone is working

questions.stem: What is a "no-show"?
options: A worker who is off sick and does not come in to work that day
A client who misses her booking without telling the salon
A service that is not shown on the salon's price list
A product that the salon keeps out of the display

questions.stem: A client calls to cancel her appointment for tomorrow. What should the receptionist do?
options: Tell her she must come anyway because it is booked
Leave the booking in the book in case she changes her mind
Charge her the full price straight away
Thank her, remove the booking, and offer her a new time

questions.stem: Why should clients be told the salon's cancellation policy when they book?
options: So they know the rules, such as the notice that is needed
So they feel worried about booking
So staff can cancel any booking without warning the client
Because the policy is a secret until a client cancels

questions.stem: When might a salon or spa ask for a deposit at the time of booking?
options: For every quick eyebrow shape, even for regular clients
Only for clients who pay in cash
For long or costly bookings, such as a bridal party
Never, as deposits are not allowed

questions.stem: What is "double booking"?
options: Booking a client for two services on the same day
Booking two clients with one worker at the same time
Writing a booking in pen and then in pencil
Booking a client for the same service two weeks in a row

questions.stem: How can double booking be avoided?
options: Use one booking system and check it before each booking
Let each worker keep her own private list on her own phone
Book clients from memory to save time at the desk
Write bookings on loose paper and file them later

questions.stem: The salon is fully booked when a walk-in client asks for a wash and set. What should the receptionist do?
options: Ask a stylist to fit her in during her lunch break without asking
Tell her to wait until someone cancels, however long it takes
Squeeze her in between two clients who are already booked
Apologise and offer the next free time or another day

questions.stem: A therapist is off sick, and her clients are booked for the day. What should the receptionist do first?
options: Wait until each client arrives to tell her
Cancel all the bookings and say nothing
Call each client to explain and offer another worker or time
Ask each of the clients to call the therapist at her home number

questions.stem: A spa uses an online booking page. What must staff still do?
options: Check new online bookings and keep the system up to date
Turn the page off whenever the spa is busy
Ask clients to phone as well, every time
Print out each booking and then delete it from the online system

questions.stem: When booking a client at the desk, why should the receptionist not read out other clients' bookings?
options: It would take up far too much of her time on a busy day
Clients' bookings are private information
Other clients would want the same times
The book is too heavy to hold up

questions.stem: Why do many salons use short codes in the appointment book, such as "MP" for manicure and pedicure?
options: So clients cannot read the book
Because the law says codes must be used
So the stylist can change the service without asking
To save space, if every staff member knows the codes

questions.stem: Why do some salons write bookings in pencil in a paper appointment book?
options: Because a pencil costs a lot less than a pen to buy
So that clients cannot read it
So changes and cancellations can be made neatly
Because ink fades in a few days

questions.stem: A client comes to the desk after her service. What should the receptionist do first?
options: Ask if she enjoyed her service and check what was done
Tell her the total and hold out the card machine
Ask her to wait while the receptionist finishes a phone chat
Give her a feedback card and ask her to fill it in at home

questions.stem: Before taking payment, why should the receptionist check the services and products against the client's service ticket?
options: So she can add a tip for the stylist to the bill without asking
So the bill is correct and nothing is missed or added by mistake
So she can decide whether the client deserves a discount
So the stylist can see how much the client spent last time

questions.stem: A client had a facial (J$7,500) and an eyebrow shape (J$1,800), and bought a cleanser (J$2,900). What is the total before tax?
A client has a voucher for 10% off services only. Her services cost J$9,300 and her product costs J$2,900. How much is the discount?
On the client's final bill, how should GCT be shown?
options: Added at the current rate, as the till or price list shows
Left off the bill if the client is a regular or a friend
Added at whatever rate the receptionist chooses for that client
Added only to cash payments, not card payments

questions.stem: Why should the receptionist offer to book the client's next appointment before she leaves?
options: So the client is not able to go to any other salon in the area
Because every client must book again by law
So the client pays for two visits at once
It keeps her look on track and fills the stylist's book

questions.stem: A client has had a relaxer touch-up. When is the next touch-up usually booked?
options: The very next day, to keep the hair straight
When the stylist advises, often after several weeks
Every week, so the hair stays very straight
Only after a year, when all the hair has grown out

questions.stem: What should the client be given or told at check-out after a chemical service?
options: A list of all the other clients booked that day
The stylist's home phone number
Aftercare advice, such as how to wash and care for the hair
A spare tub of the chemical used on her, so she can use it at home

questions.stem: At check-out, the client asks about the shampoo her stylist used. What should the receptionist do?
options: Show her the product, explain its benefits and tell her the price
Say that the shampoo is only for staff use and can never be sold
Tell her to look for it in the supermarket
Put it on her bill without asking her

questions.stem: The client's bill is ready. What should the receptionist tell her before she pays?
options: Only the total amount, since the details do not matter to clients
What the last client paid, so she can compare
How much the stylist earns from her service
Each item, its price, any discount, the GCT and the total

questions.stem: After check-out, what should be added to the client's record?
options: Her opinion of the other clients in the salon
The services, products used, any reactions and the next booking
How long she chatted with the stylist and what they talked about
Nothing, as records are only made on the first visit

questions.stem: How should a client be said goodbye to at the end of her visit?
options: Turn to serve the next client before she has even left the desk
Remind her loudly how much she spent today
Thank her by name, help with her belongings, and invite her back
Tell her to hurry because the salon is busy

questions.stem: Rohan has a client booked at 3:00 pm. His 1:30 pm client arrived 20 minutes late and needs the full 1 hour 30 minutes. If Rohan does the full service, when will he be free?
A bride books hair, make-up and nails for herself and four bridesmaids. What should the receptionist do?
options: Book all five of them at the same time with one stylist
Book them on the wedding day wherever there is a gap
Ask them to just walk in on the day and see who is free
Plan times with the staff, take a deposit and confirm it

questions.stem: A client calls to book but does not know which service she needs for her damaged hair. What should the receptionist do?
options: Book the most expensive treatment on the price list
Book her a consultation with a stylist first
Tell her to search for an answer online first
Book a relaxer, as that suits most damaged hair

questions.stem: When booking, a client says she is pregnant and would like a body massage. What should the receptionist do?
options: Book her for any massage, as pregnancy makes no difference
Refuse to book her for any service at all
Note it and ask the therapist if it is suitable
Tell her to come in and decide on the day

questions.stem: A salon charges a fee if a booking is cancelled with less than 24 hours' notice. Why do salons have a rule like this?
options: A late gap is hard to fill, so the salon loses income
So that clients are afraid to book appointments
So staff can go home early when clients cancel
Because the government sets the same fee for every salon in Jamaica

questions.stem: What is one advantage of a computer booking system over a paper book?
options: It never needs to be checked or updated by staff
It still works even when there is no power and no device at all
It lets clients see each other's private details
It can send reminders and show free times quickly

questions.stem: Why should a salon with a computer booking system keep a backup, such as a printed day list?
options: So every client can take a copy of the day's list home with her
So bookings are not lost if the power or internet fails
So the system runs faster
Because computers cannot show times

questions.stem: At check-out, a client says she cannot pay the full bill today. What should the receptionist do?
options: Shout at her in front of the other clients
Keep her handbag behind the desk until she finds the money to pay
Stay polite and call the supervisor to follow the salon's policy
Let her leave and remove the bill from the records

questions.stem: Why is check-out a good time to ask the client for feedback?
options: She is usually in a hurry, so she will give a short, quick answer
Clients only tell the truth when they are paying
It makes the queue at the desk move more slowly
The visit is fresh, and a problem can be fixed before she goes

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. You may use a calculator unless the instructor says otherwise. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: A service starts at 9:45 am and takes 1 hour 30 minutes. At what time does it end?
How many minutes are there in 2 and a quarter hours?
What do we call a booking that is kept for the same day and time every few weeks, such as every two weeks?
What do we call a space in a worker's day when no client is booked?
What word means moving a booking to a new date or time?
Reminders are often sent by SMS. What do the letters SMS stand for?
A salon is open from 8:00 am to 6:00 pm. How many hours is it open?
A facial takes 75 minutes. How many full facials can one therapist do between 9:00 am and 1:00 pm with no breaks?
What is the small card called that is given to a client to show the date and time of her next booking?
A client rebooks for 4 weeks after her visit on 3 March. On what date is her next visit?
What is the word for the end of a visit, when the client pays, rebooks and says goodbye at the desk?
What do we call a booking that a client makes herself on the salon's website or app?
A client's services come to J$5,600 and her products to J$2,450. What is the total before tax, in J$?
A bridal booking costs J$12,000. The client paid a J$3,000 deposit. How much is left to pay on the day, in J$?
What is the card or computer file called that keeps a client's details, services, products and allergies?

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how to make an appointment for a client who phones the salon or spa.
essays.modelAnswer: I answer the phone politely with the salon's name and my name. I ask which service the client wants and, if she is not sure, offer a consultation. I ask whether she has a favourite stylist or therapist, and check that the worker is trained for that service. I check the appointment book or system for a free time that allows the full length of the service, including any processing time, and offer her two or three choices. For a tint or colour, I check her record for a skin test and, if one is needed, book it at least 48 hours before, or as the maker says. I take her full name and phone number, and note any special needs, such as pregnancy or a disability. I tell her the price, the deposit if one is needed, and the cancellation policy. Finally I read all the details back to confirm, and thank her.
markingPoints: Answers politely and finds out the service needed, offering a consultation if unsure
Chooses a trained worker and a free time long enough for the full service
Checks for and books any skin test needed, often 48 hours before
Takes name, phone number and special needs, and explains price, deposit and cancellation policy
Reads the booking back to confirm it

essays.stem: Explain why correct service timing matters when booking, and how a receptionist plans a worker's day so that she does not run late.
essays.modelAnswer: Each service takes a set time, and if the receptionist books too little time, the worker runs late. Then every later client waits, gets upset or leaves, and the worker feels rushed and may make mistakes. If too much time is booked, the worker sits idle and the salon loses money. To plan the day, the receptionist uses the salon's list of service times, including consultation, processing time for chemicals and the time needed to clean and set up the station. She books only services the worker is trained to do, and blocks out her breaks, lunch and any training. She checks the book before every booking so there is no double booking. Where it is safe, she may book a short service for another client during a long processing time. She leaves a little spare time in a busy day for walk-ins or delays.
markingPoints: Explains the effects of booking too little time (delays, upset clients) or too much (lost income)
Uses the salon's service times, including consultation and processing time
Allows time for cleaning and setting up between clients
Blocks breaks and training and books only trained workers
Checks for double booking and leaves some spare time

essays.stem: Explain how skin tests and consultations affect the booking of chemical services, such as hair colour, relaxers and lash tints.
essays.modelAnswer: Chemical products can cause an allergic reaction or damage the hair, skin or scalp, so they must be booked with care. Many makers require a skin (patch) test before a tint or colour, often 48 hours before the service, and sometimes before every service or after a gap. The receptionist checks the client's record to see if a test is needed, and books the test with enough time before the service. The result is written on the record, with the date, and the service goes ahead only if the test was clear. A new client or one with a problem may also need a consultation first, so that the stylist can check the hair and scalp for cuts, irritation or past chemical damage. If anything is found, the service is not booked, and the client may be advised to see a doctor. These steps protect the client and the salon.
markingPoints: Explains the risk of reaction or damage from chemical products
Books a skin test as the maker requires, often 48 hours before
Records the result and date, and goes ahead only if it was clear
Books a consultation to check the hair and scalp for contraindications
Does not book if a problem is found and advises a doctor; explains it protects the client

essays.stem: Describe how a receptionist should deal with cancellations, late arrivals and no-shows, and why salons have policies for them.
essays.modelAnswer: When a client cancels, the receptionist thanks her for letting the salon know, removes the booking so the time is free, and offers her a new time. If the salon keeps a waiting list, she calls the next client to offer the free time. When a client arrives late, she checks with the worker how much time is left. She explains politely and offers a shorter service, waiting for the next free time, or a new booking, so other clients are not kept waiting. When a client does not turn up, she tries to contact her, marks a no-show on her record, and follows the salon's policy, which may mean keeping a deposit or charging a fee. Salons have these policies because an empty time cannot be sold again, and late arrivals make every later client wait. The policy must be explained when the client books so that it is fair.
markingPoints: Cancellation: thanks the client, frees the time, offers a new booking and fills the gap if possible
Late arrival: checks the time left and offers a shorter service, a wait or a new booking
No-show: tries to contact her, records it and follows the policy (deposit or fee)
Explains that empty times lose income and lateness delays other clients
Says the policy must be explained at booking to be fair

essays.stem: Compare a paper appointment book with a computer or online booking system. Give at least two advantages and one disadvantage of each.
essays.modelAnswer: A paper appointment book is cheap and simple to use, and it works without power or the internet. Staff can see the whole day at a glance. But it can only be in one place, it is easy to make it messy with changes, and bookings can be lost if a page is torn or the book is lost. It cannot send reminders, and finding past bookings takes time. A computer or online booking system can show free times quickly, warn of double bookings, send text or email reminders to clients who agree, and let clients book themselves online at any time. It can also keep client records and print reports. But it costs money, needs power, a device and often the internet, and staff need training to use it. It must be protected with a password because it holds private data, and a backup, such as a printed day list, is needed in case it fails.
markingPoints: Paper: cheap, simple, works without power, day seen at a glance
Paper disadvantages: messy changes, can be lost, no reminders, slow to search
Computer: quick free times, double-booking warnings, reminders, online booking, records
Computer disadvantages: cost, needs power and internet, training
Mentions password protection and a backup for a computer system

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how to check out a client at the end of her visit.
essays.modelAnswer: When the client comes to the desk, I greet her by name, ask if she enjoyed her service and check that she is happy with the result. If she has a concern, I listen and call the stylist or supervisor before going on. I check her service ticket against the booking to see which services and products she had. I ask if she would like any home-care products her stylist recommended. Then I prepare the bill, with each item, any discount, voucher or deposit, and GCT at the current rate, and I tell her each item and the total. I take the payment, give her the correct change or card slip and a receipt. I offer to book her next appointment and give her an appointment card. I make sure she has her aftercare advice. I update her record. Finally I help her with her belongings, thank her and invite her back.
markingPoints: Greets the client and checks she is happy with the service
Checks the service ticket and offers recommended products
Prepares and explains an accurate bill with discounts, deposits and GCT
Takes payment correctly and gives a receipt
Rebooks, gives aftercare, updates the record and says goodbye warmly

essays.stem: Explain how to prepare an accurate bill at check-out for a client who had several services, bought a product, has a discount voucher and paid a deposit.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the client's service ticket and the booking to list every service she actually had, for example a manicure, a pedicure and a paraffin wax foot treatment, with the price of each from the current price list. I add any product she is buying, with its price. Then I check her discount voucher: that it is the salon's own, in date and not used, and what it covers, such as 10% off services only. I work out the discount on the right items and take it off. Next I add GCT at the current rate, as the till or the salon's policy shows. Then I take off the deposit she paid when she booked, after checking the deposit receipt or record. I check my sums again, or let the till work them out and check it. Finally I explain each line to the client before she pays.
markingPoints: Lists every service from the ticket and booking, with current prices
Adds the product being bought
Checks the voucher is valid and applies the discount only to the right items
Adds GCT at the current rate and takes off the deposit after checking it
Checks the sums and explains each line to the client

essays.stem: Explain why rebooking, aftercare advice and home-care products are offered at check-out, and how a receptionist can offer them without pushing the client.
essays.modelAnswer: Rebooking at check-out helps the client keep her look, for example a touch-up before the new growth shows or nails filled before they lift, and it fills the worker's book ahead of time. Aftercare advice helps the client keep the result at home and avoid problems, such as washing a relaxer too soon or picking at gel polish. Home-care products help her follow that advice, and they add to the salon's sales. The receptionist should link each offer to what the stylist advised: "Your stylist suggests a touch-up in about eight weeks. Shall I book that for you?" She can explain how a product helps, and let the client try a tester. She should accept a "no" politely, give an appointment card or a leaflet, and invite the client to call when she is ready. Honest, helpful offers build trust; pressure drives clients away.
markingPoints: Rebooking keeps the client's look and fills the book
Aftercare advice helps her keep the result and avoid problems
Home-care products support the advice and add to sales
Links offers to the stylist's advice and explains the benefit
Accepts a no politely and does not pressure the client

essays.stem: A client wants to book a spa day for herself and three friends: a massage, a facial and a pedicure each, followed by lunch. Explain how you would plan and book it.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would take the main client's name and phone number and the date she wants, and ask about any allergies, medical conditions or pregnancy in the group, so the therapists can check the treatments are suitable. I would work out the total time: each person has three treatments, so I need to plan who goes where and when. I would check which therapists are trained and free that day, and draw up a timetable that rotates the four guests through the treatment rooms, so no therapist or room is double booked and each guest has short breaks. I would book lunch at a time when all four are free. I would tell her the package price, the deposit needed and the cancellation policy, and take the deposit. I would send her the timetable in writing, and send a reminder a few days before. I would also tell the therapists so they can prepare.
markingPoints: Takes contact details and asks about allergies, medical conditions and pregnancy
Works out the total time and the order of treatments for each guest
Checks trained, free therapists and rooms with no double booking
Explains the price, takes a deposit and explains the cancellation policy
Confirms in writing, sends a reminder and briefs the staff

essays.stem: Explain what should be recorded about a client after her visit, and how the salon keeps those records private.
essays.modelAnswer: After each visit, the client's record should be updated with the date, the services she had and the worker who did them. For chemical services, the products, the colour or strength, the processing time and the result should be noted, so they can be repeated or changed next time. Any skin test result, reaction, allergy or contraindication must be written down clearly. The record should also show the products she bought, her next booking, and any preferences or comments, including a complaint and how it was solved. Her phone number should be checked. To keep records private, paper cards are kept in a closed file or locked drawer, and computer records are protected with a password and the screen is locked when the desk is left. Details are never read out or shown to other clients, and they are never shared or sold, as Jamaica's data protection law requires.
markingPoints: Records the date, services and worker
Records chemical details: products, strength, timing and result
Records skin tests, reactions and allergies clearly
Records products bought, next booking, preferences and any complaint
Keeps records locked or password-protected and never shares them

practical1.title: Book a day's appointments for a salon and spa from client phone calls
practical1.brief: As a group, run the bookings for one day at a salon and spa. The assessor gives you a blank appointment page with columns for four workers (for example a stylist, a second stylist, a nail technician and a beauty therapist), the list of what each worker is trained to do, their breaks, and the salon's service times and price list in J$. The assessor also gives booking request cards. Take turns so that every member takes at least three phone calls as the receptionist, while the others play the clients and one member checks the page after each call. The calls must include: an ordinary booking; a hair colour for a new client who needs a skin test 48 hours before; a client who asks for a stylist who is not trained for that service; a cancellation, with the time offered to a client on the waiting list; a client who wants to move her booking; and a bridal group booking with a deposit. For each call, the receptionist checks the page, offers suitable times, takes the details, explains the price and cancellation policy, writes the booking neatly and reads it back. At the end, the group writes a reminder message for each client booked. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A blank appointment page (or the Centre's practice booking screen) with four worker columns
Workers' skills list, breaks, service times and price list in J$
Booking request cards from the assessor
Two phones, or chairs back to back for the calls
Pencils, erasers, pens, appointment cards and a waiting list sheet
photos: The blank appointment page with breaks blocked out
Each member taking a call and writing the booking (hands, phone and page only)
The skin test booked at least 48 hours before the colour
The cancellation crossed out neatly and the time given to the waiting-list client
The bridal group booking with the deposit noted
The finished appointment page for the day
The reminder messages written for the clients
checklist: Answered politely and found out the service the client needed
Booked a worker trained for the service, for the full service time
Booked the skin test with enough time before the colour service
Took the client's name, phone number and any special needs
Explained the price, any deposit and the cancellation policy
Read the booking back to the client to confirm it
Handled the cancellation or change neatly, with no double booking
safety: Use only made-up client names and phone numbers
Keep the appointment page and practice screen private from people outside the group
Keep phone cables and bags out of the walkway
Sit with a straight back and take short breaks from the screen

practical2.title: Check out clients at the end of their services
practical2.brief: As a group, run the check-out desk of a salon and spa at the end of their clients' services. The assessor gives you a completed appointment page, a service ticket for each client, the price list in J$, client record cards, aftercare leaflets and some retail products. Take turns so that every member checks out at least two clients, while the others play the clients and one member checks each bill. The clients must include: one who buys a product her stylist recommended; one with a 10% discount voucher for services only; one who paid a deposit when booking; one who is not happy with part of her service; and one who wants to rebook. For each client, the member greets her, checks she is happy, checks the ticket against the booking, prepares the bill with GCT at the rate the assessor gives, explains each line, takes the payment with training money or practice slips, gives a receipt, offers to rebook and gives an appointment card, gives the aftercare leaflet, updates the record card, and says goodbye. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Photos show hands, papers and the desk, not faces. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A completed appointment page and a service ticket for each client
Price list in J$, discount vouchers and deposit receipts
Client record cards, aftercare leaflets and appointment cards
A few retail products with testers
Training money, a cash tray, practice card slips, receipt book and calculator
photos: The check-out desk set up with the tickets, price list and leaflets
Each member checking a service ticket against the appointment page
Each member's completed bill, showing the discount, deposit and GCT
The payment being taken and the receipt given (hands only)
An appointment card filled in for a rebooking
A client record card updated after check-out
checklist: Greeted the client and checked she was happy with her service
Dealt politely with the unhappy client and called the supervisor
Checked the service ticket against the booking
Prepared an accurate bill, with the discount, deposit and given GCT rate correct
Explained each line of the bill before payment
Took the payment correctly and gave a receipt
Offered to rebook, gave an appointment card and the aftercare leaflet
Updated the client record accurately and said goodbye warmly
safety: Use only training money, practice slips and made-up client details
Keep record cards private and put them away after use
Use testers with a clean spatula or pump, and ask about allergies first
Wash or sanitise hands after handling money
